doc.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18

title: Tuts Johnson's band in Baton Rouge with Buddy Petit
summary: Darensbourg played in Tuts Johnson's band at about 16, which he rates above many New Orleans bands; Buddy Petit came from New Orleans to play trumpet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: was your story? Well, they got funny names in Baton Rouge, but you ought to know that anyway. So, uh, was there much, much music in Baton Rouge? They had a lot of music in Baton Rouge. When I was about 16 years old, I played in a band in Baton Rouge called, uh, Tuts Johnson's Band. Yeah. And
personally, I think that was one of the best bands ever to come out of Louisiana. Really? Yes. You
mean, you mean as good as a good New Orleans band? Better than a lot of those New Orleans bands. That
band used to go to New Orleans and cut a lot of those New Orleans bands. Buddy P.T. was the trumpet player in that band. Oh, yeah. You remember Buddy P.T.? Yeah. Yeah. So, what was he

doing with Baton Rouge? He came from New Orleans to work in this band. Oh, yeah? What? That must have been about, about 1922 or something? Just about. That's fine. What were you playing? What instruments? Clarinet. My teacher played in the band. When did you first become interested
